name: General Psychiatry
description: Comprehensive diagnosis and pharmacological management of the full spectrum of mental health disorders including mood, psychotic, and anxiety disorders. Encompasses both inpatient and outpatient clinical evaluation and treatment planning.

name: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT)
description: A structured, evidence-based psychotherapy that identifies and restructures maladaptive thought patterns and behaviors to alleviate psychological distress. Widely applied for depression, anxiety, OCD, and PTSD.

name: Addiction Medicine & Substance Use Disorders
description: Medical specialty focused on the prevention, evaluation, diagnosis, and treatment of substance use disorders including alcohol, opioid, stimulant, and polysubstance dependencies. Includes medically assisted treatment (MAT) protocols.

name: Adolescent & Child Psychiatry
description: Specialized psychiatric care for children and teenagers presenting with neurodevelopmental, mood, anxiety, and behavioral disorders. Integrates family-centered approaches with pharmacological and psychotherapeutic interventions.

name: Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR)
description: An evidence-based, trauma-focused psychotherapy protocol that uses bilateral stimulation to help patients reprocess distressing memories and reduce PTSD symptomatology. Recognized by the WHO and APA as a first-line trauma treatment.

name: Forensic Psychiatry
description: Intersection of psychiatry and law involving evaluation of individuals involved in legal proceedings, determination of criminal responsibility, and management of mentally disordered offenders. Includes competency and risk assessments.

name: Geriatric Psychiatry
description: Specialized psychiatric care for older adults (65+) addressing dementia, late-life depression, anxiety, and psychotic disorders. Focuses on the neuropsychiatric sequelae of aging and chronic medical comorbidities.

name: Trauma-Informed Therapy
description: A clinical framework and therapeutic approach that recognizes the widespread impact of trauma and integrates this knowledge into all aspects of treatment to support healing and avoid re-traumatization. Applicable across PTSD, complex trauma, and adverse childhood experiences (ACEs).

name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
description: A comprehensive, evidence-based behavioral treatment originally developed for borderline personality disorder, focusing on skills training in mindfulness, distress tolerance, emotion regulation, and interpersonal effectiveness. Effective for suicidality and chronic self-harm.

name: Eating Disorders & Body Image
description: Multidisciplinary treatment for anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa, binge eating disorder, and ARFID, integrating medical stabilization, nutritional rehabilitation, and evidence-based psychotherapy. Emphasizes long-term recovery and relapse prevention.

name: Psychoanalytic & Psychodynamic Therapy
description: Long-term therapeutic approach exploring unconscious processes, early developmental experiences, and relational patterns that contribute to current psychological distress. Aims to foster insight, self-awareness, and character change.

name: Couples & Relationship Therapy
description: Therapeutic interventions designed to help couples identify and resolve conflict, improve communication patterns, and strengthen relational bonds. Draws from Emotionally Focused Therapy (EFT) and the Gottman Method.

name: Family Systems Therapy
description: A psychotherapeutic approach that addresses the family unit as an interconnected emotional system, working to resolve dysfunctional patterns, improve communication, and support individual members within the systemic context.

name: Neuropsychiatry
description: A subspecialty at the interface of neurology and psychiatry, managing psychiatric manifestations of neurological conditions such as TBI, epilepsy, Parkinson's disease, and stroke. Integrates neuroimaging, cognitive assessment, and pharmacotherapy.

name: Sleep Medicine & Sleep Disorders
description: Diagnosis and treatment of sleep-related disorders including insomnia, obstructive sleep apnea, narcolepsy, and parasomnias, with an emphasis on their bidirectional relationship with psychiatric conditions. Uses polysomnography and CBT-I protocols.

name: Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy (MBCT)
description: An evidence-based group psychotherapy combining mindfulness meditation practices with cognitive therapy techniques to prevent depressive relapse and reduce ruminative thought patterns. Clinically indicated for recurrent major depressive disorder.

name: Grief & Bereavement Counseling
description: Specialized counseling that supports individuals navigating loss, complicated grief, and bereavement through evidence-based models including the Dual Process Model and Prolonged Grief Disorder treatment protocols.

name: OCD & Obsessive-Compulsive Spectrum Disorders
description: Specialized treatment of Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder and related conditions (BDD, hoarding, trichotillomania) using Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP) and inference-based CBT. Includes pharmacological augmentation strategies.

name: Bipolar Disorder & Mood Stabilization
description: Expert management of Bipolar I, II, and cyclothymic disorders through mood-stabilizing pharmacotherapy, psychoeducation, and lifestyle interventions. Focuses on relapse prevention and long-term functional recovery.

name: Anxiety & Panic Disorders
description: Comprehensive evaluation and treatment of generalized anxiety disorder, panic disorder, social anxiety, agoraphobia, and specific phobias through integrated pharmacotherapy and psychotherapy approaches.

name: Perinatal & Reproductive Psychiatry
description: Specialized psychiatric care addressing mental health conditions during pregnancy and the postpartum period, including perinatal depression, anxiety, and postpartum psychosis. Balances pharmacological safety with maternal and fetal wellbeing.

name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
description: A third-wave behavioral therapy that uses acceptance, mindfulness, and values-based committed action strategies to increase psychological flexibility and reduce experiential avoidance. Applicable across a wide range of mental health presentations.

name: Somatic & Body-Based Therapy
description: A body-centered therapeutic approach that addresses the physical manifestations of psychological trauma and stress stored in the body. Incorporates techniques from Somatic Experiencing (SE) and Sensorimotor Psychotherapy.

name: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) & Neurodevelopmental Disorders
description: Comprehensive diagnostic evaluation and therapeutic management of Autism Spectrum Disorder, ADHD, and other neurodevelopmental conditions across the lifespan. Integrates behavioral, developmental, and pharmacological interventions.

name: Psychosis & Schizophrenia Spectrum Disorders
description: Advanced treatment of schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, delusional disorder, and first-episode psychosis using evidence-based antipsychotic pharmacotherapy, Coordinated Specialty Care (CSC), and cognitive remediation.

name: Group Psychotherapy
description: Facilitation of structured therapeutic group experiences leveraging interpersonal learning, universality, and group cohesion to address shared psychological concerns. Based on Yalom's therapeutic factors and interpersonal process group principles.

name: School-Based & Pediatric Counseling
description: Counseling services tailored to children and adolescents in educational settings, addressing academic stress, behavioral issues, social difficulties, and early mental health intervention. Collaborates with families and school systems.

name: Cultural & Multicultural Psychology
description: A culturally responsive clinical approach that acknowledges the influence of race, ethnicity, immigration, and acculturation on mental health presentation and treatment outcomes. Integrates culturally adapted evidence-based therapies.

name: Clinical Neuropsychology
description: Comprehensive neuropsychological assessment of cognitive functioning including memory, attention, executive function, and language following brain injury, neurological disease, or neurodegenerative conditions. Informs rehabilitation planning.

name: Sex Therapy & Sexual Health
description: Specialized clinical counseling addressing sexual dysfunctions, gender identity, intimacy disorders, and paraphilias within an evidence-based, non-judgmental therapeutic framework. Incorporates both individual and couples modalities.

name: Chronic Pain & Health Psychology
description: Psychological treatment of chronic pain conditions using CBT-pain protocols, acceptance-based strategies, and biofeedback to reduce pain-related disability, catastrophizing, and psychiatric comorbidities.

name: Sport & Performance Psychology
description: Applied psychological services for athletes and high-performance individuals addressing performance anxiety, burnout, identity, and career transitions. Uses mental skills training and mindfulness-based interventions.

name: Vocational & Occupational Counseling
description: Career counseling and psychological support for individuals experiencing work-related stress, burnout, career transitions, and occupational impairment due to mental health conditions. Integrates vocational rehabilitation principles.

name: Electroconvulsive Therapy (ECT) & Neuromodulation
description: Specialized administration and monitoring of ECT, TMS, and emerging neuromodulation therapies for treatment-resistant depression, severe mania, and catatonia. Includes pre-treatment evaluation and post-treatment neuropsychological monitoring.

name: LGBTQ+ Affirming Therapy
description: Culturally affirming therapeutic support for lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer, and intersex individuals addressing minority stress, identity development, discrimination-related trauma, and family rejection.

name: Play Therapy & Expressive Arts
description: A developmentally appropriate therapeutic modality for children that uses play, art, and creative expression as the primary medium of communication and healing. Addresses behavioral disorders, attachment disruptions, and childhood trauma.

name: Narrative Therapy
description: A postmodern therapeutic approach that helps individuals re-author their life stories, separating their identity from their problems and highlighting alternative narratives of competence and resilience.

name: Crisis Intervention & Suicide Prevention
description: Specialized clinical skills for acute risk assessment, safety planning, and stabilization of individuals in psychiatric crisis. Includes suicide risk stratification using validated tools such as the Columbia Protocol (C-SSRS).

name: Biofeedback & Neurofeedback Therapy
description: Technology-assisted therapeutic technique that trains individuals to regulate physiological processes (heart rate variability, EEG brainwave activity) to improve self-regulation, reduce anxiety, and address ADHD symptoms.

name: Clinical Psychopharmacology
description: Advanced expertise in the use, monitoring, and optimization of psychotropic medications across all psychiatric diagnostic categories. Emphasizes polypharmacy management, drug-drug interactions, and treatment-resistant cases.

name: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) Treatment
description: Specialized delivery of first-line PTSD therapies including Prolonged Exposure (PE), Cognitive Processing Therapy (CPT), and EMDR within military, civilian, and disaster-response populations.

name: Personality Disorders
description: Expert clinical management of Cluster A, B, and C personality disorders using transdiagnostic approaches including Schema Therapy, Transference-Focused Psychotherapy (TFP), and DBT. Emphasizes long-term therapeutic alliance and functional recovery.

name: Motivational Interviewing (MI)
description: A collaborative, person-centered counseling method designed to strengthen an individual's motivation for and commitment to behavior change. Widely used in substance use, chronic disease management, and treatment engagement contexts.

name: Positive Psychology & Wellbeing Coaching
description: A strengths-based counseling approach grounded in the science of wellbeing, resilience, and flourishing. Utilizes PERMA framework interventions to enhance life satisfaction, meaning, and psychological capital.

name: Telepsychiatry & Digital Mental Health
description: Delivery of psychiatric assessments, medication management, and psychotherapy via synchronous and asynchronous digital platforms. Specializes in expanding access to care for rural, underserved, and mobility-impaired populations.

name: Anger Management & Impulse Control
description: Structured therapeutic programs addressing anger dysregulation, intermittent explosive disorder, and impulse control deficits through cognitive restructuring, skills training, and emotional regulation techniques.

name: Dissociative Disorders & DID Therapy
description: Specialized psychotherapy for dissociative identity disorder, depersonalization/derealization, and other dissociative conditions using phase-based trauma treatment, internal family systems (IFS), and stabilization techniques.

name: Community Mental Health & Psychosocial Rehabilitation
description: Recovery-oriented services supporting individuals with severe and persistent mental illness in achieving community integration, independent living, and social inclusion. Employs Assertive Community Treatment (ACT) and psychosocial rehabilitation models.

name: Clinical Hypnotherapy
description: Evidence-informed therapeutic use of hypnotic induction and suggestion to facilitate access to unconscious material, alleviate phobias, manage chronic pain, and address habit disorders under a licensed clinical framework.

name: Existential & Humanistic Therapy
description: A philosophical approach to psychotherapy that addresses existential concerns such as meaning, freedom, mortality, and isolation as sources of psychological distress. Draws from Viktor Frankl's Logotherapy and Carl Rogers' Person-Centered Therapy.
